3D graphics (WebGL) are switched off in: 3D grafik (WebGL) de ɔf na dis brɔuza. On hadwae akselereshɔn na di brawza sɛtin ɛn stat di brawza bak fɔ si di 3D hal.
A “Setu” coin with a bull on the obverse: Wan “Setu” kɔyn we gɛt kaw na di fɔs pat. Di wɔd Setu — di brij fɔ go na Lanka, na Rameswaram — de pan kɔyn dɛn we di let mɛdival Tamil rula dɛn na di Jafna kiŋdɔm; di couchant bull, Shiva’s Nandi, na dɛn kɔmɔn tin.
A burial urn of the kind that made Adich: Wan bɛrin urn we tan lɛk we mek Adichanallur gɛt nem. Dɛn bin de put di wan dɛn we dɔn day — ɔ dɛn bon dɛn we dɛn gɛda — insay dɛn kayn urn dɛn de wit grev guds ɛn bɛr dɛn na di grɔn we gɛt grɔn ɔp di Thamirabarani. Di urn dɛn na dairekt link to di முதுமக்கள் தாழி fɔ Sangam poem.
A catalogue of the coins issued by the C: Wan katalog fɔ di kɔyn dɛn we di Chera, Chola, ɛn Pandya kiŋ dɛn bin gi, wit dɛn kiŋ in mak dɛn we gɛt di bɔw, di tayga, ɛn di fish.
A ceramic vessel from Adichanallur. Smal: Wan sɛramik bɔtul we kɔmɔt na Adichanallur. Dɛn bin de put smɔl smɔl pɔt dɛn lɛk dis insay ɔ nia di bɛrin urn dɛn, sɔntɛm dɛn bin de ol it, wata ɔ ɔfrin fɔ di wan dɛn we dɔn day — wan smɔl tin we dɛn biliv pan di Ayɔn Ij biliv pan wan waka we pas day.
A chariot for a creeper, a shawl for a p: Wan chariɔt fɔ wan kripa, wan shawl fɔ wan pikɔk, wan frut we de gi layf fɔ pɔsin we de rayt poem: di gift dɛn we di pipul dɛn we de kam fɔ it kin gɛt we pipul dɛn sabi pas ɔl kin luk lɛk se dɛn nɔ pɔsibul, ɛn na dat na dɛn pɔynt. Kodai madam na jenarositi so bɔku dat di pɔsin we gi am nɔ de kɔl di gift in yus — sɔri-at we dɛn de ɛkstɛnd to animal, plant ɛn lanin ɔl tu.
A Chera coin in the collection of the Na: Wan Chera kɔyn we de na di kɔlekɛshɔn na di Napier Miusiɔm, Thiruvananthapuram. Chera kɔyn dɛn kin gɛt di bɔw ɛn aro, we na di dynasty’s emblem, ɛn bɔku fɔs fɔs ɛgzampul dɛn kɔmɔt frɔm Karur, di Chera sɛnta pan di Amaravathi.
A chieftain of the Ay line in the southe: Wan bigman na di Ay layn na di sawt pat na di il kɔntri na di Podiyil (Pothigai). Wan tradishɔn we bɔku pipul dɛn sabi de tɔk bɔt aw i bin de gi wan valyu klos to wan gɔd, we dɛn kin kɔl Shiva — gi as divoshɔn ɛn bak as fri-an.
A chieftain of the Malaiyaman lineage, o: Wan chifman we kɔmɔt na di Malaiyaman layn, we kɔmɔt na di kɔntri we de rawnd Mullur ɛn Tirukkoyilur, bin mɛmba fɔ in munificence to poet ɛn to ɔl di wan dɛn we bin de kam to am. Di ples we i bin gɛt bitwin di sɛvin pipul dɛn we bin de sɔpɔt am, sho se dɛn bin de mɛzhɔ di ɔnɔ we rula gɛt bay we i de gi bɔku tin dɛn jɔs lɛk aw dɛn kin mɛzhɔ di say we i de.
A Chola coin carrying Pandya royal insig: Wan Chola kɔyn we gɛt Pandya kiŋ insignia. We di Cholas dɛn briŋ di Pandya kɔntri ɔnda dɛn rul, dɛn put di Pandya fish nia dɛn yon tayga — wan emblem fɔ kɔnkrit we dɛn slap insay mɛtal.
A city where literature, royal patronage: Wan siti usay buk, kiŋ in sɔpɔt, rilijɔn ɛn layf na di siti dɔn mit fɔ lɛk tu tawzin ia so.
A coin of Kulottunga Chola bearing the t: Wan kɔyn we Kulottunga Chola gɛt we gɛt di taytul “Malai Nadu konda Chola” — di Chola dɛn we tek di hil kɔntri, dat na di Chera land. Chola kiŋ dɛn bin de prich se dɛn win bay taytul dɛn we dɛn bin de kɔt pan dɛn kɔyn dɛn ɛn bak we dɛn kɔt insay dɛn tin dɛn we dɛn rayt.
A coin of Kulottunga I (1070–1120 CE), w: Wan kɔyn we Kulottunga I (1070–1120 C.E.), we bin mek di Chola ɛn Istan Chalukya layn dɛn jɔyn an ɛn rul wan pan di Chola rul dɛn we bin lɔng pas ɔl ɛn we bin gɛt bɔku prɔpati. In kɔyn dɛn kɔntinyu di established Chola tayp dɛn wit in nem insay Nagari.
A coin of Rajaraja I. His copper coins o: Wan kɔyn we Rajaraja I. In kɔpa kɔyn dɛn we tan lɛk kiŋ we tinap ɛn we sidɔm, we dɛn bin kam wit afta i win di nɔt pat na Sri Lanka, bin de ɔlsay na di tu say dɛn na di si ɛn dɛn bin de falamakata dɛn fɔ lɔng lɔng tɛm.
A coin of the Jaffna kingdom showing a h: Wan kɔyn na di Jafna kiŋdɔm we de sho wan ɔs wit fish. Di Tamil kiŋ dɛn na Jafna (13th–17th sɛntiwɔd) bin gi kɔyn dɛn insay wan Sawt Indian tradishɔn, we bin mɛmba di tayt tayt we bin de akɔdin to di Palk Stret.
A coin of the Kongu Cheras, the Chera li: Wan kɔyn fɔ di Kongu Cheras, di Chera layn we bin de rul di Kongu kɔntri na di wɛst Tamil rijɔn (arawnd di Coimbatore, Erode ɛn Karur tide) — di sem rijyɔn we dɔn gi bɔku bɔku Roman kɔyn dɛn.
A crowned, moustached figure in profile,: Wan figa we gɛt krawn, we gɛt mɔstaz ɛn we wɛr prɔfayl, we wɛr jakit we gɛt jɔlɔs ɛn skaf we de flɔ, de es wan stik we gɛt fɛda. Dɛn drɔ di fes ɛn an dɛn wit fayn blak layn pan pale grɔn ɛn dɛn was di klos dɛn wit ɔch, pink ɛn grɛn — wan stɔdi we tan lɛk pɔtrɛt bɔt kɔt dres insay tɛmpul peint.
A detail of the painted ceiling of the J: Wan ditel bɔt di siling we dɛn dɔn pent na di Jain kev shrine na Sittanavasal: pink lotus dɛn we de opin bitwin grɔn pad dɛn, wan animal we de waka na di wata ɛn wan figa we de gɛda flawa dɛn. Bɔku tɛm dɛn kin rid di pul as di lotus moat na di samavasarana, we na di asɛmbli na ɛvin usay wan Jain Tirthankara kin prich, wit di fetful pipul dɛn we kin gɛda flawa dɛn fɔ gi.
A funerary vessel from the burial cairns: Wan bɛrin bot we kɔmɔt na di bɛrin kech dɛn na di Nilgiri il dɛn, in lid krawn wit figa dɛn we dɛn mek lɛk se dɛn de du am. Nayntin sɛnti-ɛgzampul pipul dɛn we bin de dig di Nilgiri kech dɛn bin fɛn bɔku pan dɛn kayn lid dɛn ya we dɛn bin put pipul, animal ɛn rayda dɛn pan — smɔl smɔl tin dɛn we dɛn mek wit kle we kin sho di layf ɛn di stetɔs we di wan dɛn we dɔn day gɛt.
A garland of about a hundred and fifty a: Wan garland we gɛt lɛk wan ɔndrɛd ɛn fifti akam vas dɛn we Kanimethaviyar rayt, lɛk tati fɔ ɛni wan pan di fayv land skay dɛn.
A gold coin of Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE),: Wan gold kɔyn we Rajaraja I (985–1014 C.E.), we bil di big tɛmpul na Thanjavur bin mek. I sho di klashik Chola royal emblem: di tayga we sidɔm we tu Pandya fish dɛn flank, ɔnda wan parasol fɔ sovereignty, wit di kiŋ in nem insay Nagari — di Chola dɛn de tɔk se dɛn de rul di sawt.
A gold half-kahavanu of Virarajendra Cho: Wan gold af-kahavanu we Virarajendra Chola (1063–1070 C.E.) bin mek. Kahavanu (frɔm kahapana) na bin gold denomineshɔn na Sri Lanka, ɛn Chola gold we dɛn slap to dis standad de sho di tɛm we Chola dɛn bin de rul di ayland.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiya: Wan gayd poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar rayt. Wan bard wit di big yazh de gayd am to Thondaiman Ilanthiraiyan na Kanchi; along di we di poem de peint klia klia tin dɛn bɔt vilej dɛn, pɔt dɛn, ɛn pipul dɛn.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Mudath: Wan gayd poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Mudathama Kanniyar rayt. Wan bard we de ple drɔm (porunar) we dɛn dɔn gɛt bɔku blɛsin, de gayd in kɔmpin bard to di Chola kiŋ we gɛt fri-an we nem Karikal Valavan.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Nallur: Wan gayd poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Nallur Nathathanar rayt. Wan bard we de ple di smɔl yazh (harp) de lid ɔda wan to di chif Nalliyakkodan, we de tɔk bɔt di prɔblɛm dɛn we po bad dɛn kin gɛt ɛn di wam we pɔsin we gɛt fri-an kin gɛt.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Perunk: Wan gayd poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Perunkausikanar rayt. Dɛn kin gayd di wan dɛn we de ple waka we de waka (koothar) to di chif Nannan; dɛn kin sɛlibret di poem fɔ we i kech di bɔku bɔku sawnd dɛn we di mawnten dɛn kin mek.
A large storage jar associated with Adic: Wan big stɔrɔj ​​jɔg we gɛt fɔ du wit Adichanallur. Dɛn bin de kip tin dɛn we dɛn kin yuz fɔ mek tin dɛn fɔ it, wata ɛn ɔda tin dɛn we dɛn kin yuz fɔ mek tin dɛn; na say dɛn we dɛn kin bɛr pipul dɛn, bɔtul dɛn we gɛt dis saiz kin bi bak lɛk ɔn. Di wɔd “dolio” de mek wi mɛmba di dolium, we na di big tin we dɛn bin de kip tin dɛn na di Roman wɔl.
A large, round-bellied funerary urn from: Wan big, rawnd bɛlɛ fɔ bɛr pɔsin we kɔmɔt na Adichanallur. Urn lɛk dis kin tinap lɔng pas pikin, ɛn fɔ mek dɛn nid fɔ gɛt bɔku skil: Sangam poet dɛn kin adrɛs di pɔsin we de mek pɔt we mek ɔn dɛn lɛk கலம்செய் கோவே — “O king among potters”.
A lead coin from Andipatti bearing a leg: Wan lid kɔyn frɔm Andipatti we gɛt wan lay lay stori insay Tamil-Brahmi. Apat frɔm di tri kiŋ dɛn we dɛn bin dɔn krawn, di lokal chif dɛn we bin de insay di Sangam tɛm bin de pul kɔyn dɛn we dɛn mek wit lid ɛn kɔpa, ɛn di Tamil-Brahmi lay lay stori dɛn bɔt dɛn bin de ɛp fɔ put nem to dɛn rula dɛn ya.
A line drawing of the vimana and a pilla: Wan layn we dɛn drɔ di vimana ɛn wan ol we gɛt pila dɛn na di Brihadisvara Tɛmpl.
A love poem of the Ten Idylls by Kapilar: Wan lɔv poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Kapilar rayt, we dɛn sɛt na di mawnten (kurinji) land skay. Tradishɔn se dɛn rayt am fɔ tich wan kiŋ na di nɔt di fayn fayn tin dɛn we Tamil lɔv poem dɛn gɛt; i gɛt nem fɔ gi naynti-nayn flawa dɛn nem.
A modern artist’s imagining of a busy ha: Wan mɔdan atis in imajin fɔ wan bizi haba we gɛt ship, makit ɛn tawa, afta di diskripshɔn dɛn na Silappathikaram ɛn Pattinappalai. I nɔto pruf fɔ sho aw di siti bin rili tan.
A modern sketch imagining ships and buil: Wan skech we dɛn mek tide we de imajin ship dɛn ɛn bildin dɛn na di ol pɔt. Lɛk ɛvri rikostrɔkshɔn fɔ Puhar, i de intaprit di diskripshɔn dɛn we dɛn rayt; di ful layout fɔ di pɔt nɔ no.
A name linked with Nedunalvadai and Tiru: Wan nem we gɛt fɔ du wit Nedunalvadai ɛn Tirumurukarruppatai insay di Tɛn Idylls — pan ɔl we i kin bi fɔ mɔ pas wan pɔyt akɔdin to difrɛn tɛm dɛn. Leta lay lay stori tɔk bɔt aw i nɔ gri fɔ gi in jɔjmɛnt fɔ wan poem ivin to Shiva na di Pandya kɔt: na sayn fɔ intɛlektual kɔrej, nɔto istri ivin.
A palm-leaf manuscript from the museum’s: Wan manuskrip we dɛn mek wit pam lif frɔm di tin dɛn we di myuziɔm dɔn gɛda.
A Pandya coin of the “massa” type. Massa: Wan Pandya kɔyn we gɛt di kayn “massa”. Massa na di nem we dɛn gi di mɛdival kɔpa kɔyn dɛn we de sho wan figa we tinap na wan say ɛn wan figa we sidɔm na di ɔda say — wan tayp we di Chola dɛn bin spre ɛn we di Pandya dɛn ɛn di kiŋ dɛn na Sri Lanka bin kɔntinyu.
A Pandya coin showing a standing king wi: Wan Pandya kɔyn we de sho wan kiŋ we tinap wit di fish ɛmblem. Di figa fɔ wan rula we tinap, we di Chola kɔpa kɔyn dɛn bin mek pipul dɛn sabi, na in di Pandya dɛn bin tek am we dɛn pawa kam bak insay di 13t sɛntinari.
A Pandya coin with the twin fish and a b: Wan Pandya kɔyn wit di twin fish ɛn wan kaw. Di fish we dɛn tu tu bin bi di Pandya ɛmblem we bin de sote go, dɛn kɔt am na di Madurai ban dɛn na di poem dɛn ɛn dɛn bin slap am pan kɔyn dɛn fɔ pas wan tawzin ia.
A pillared hall today: Wan ol we gɛt pila dɛn tide
A pillared mandapam: Wan mandapam we gɛt pila dɛn
A pipeline of terracotta rings, set one: Wan paip we dɛn mek wit tɛrakota ring dɛn, we dɛn put wan ɔp di ɔda wan insay 4 taya, we dɛn bin de na do we dɛn bin de dig di Kɔrkai. Faya-kle paip ɛn ring wɛl dɛn lɛk dis bin de kɛr ɛn dreyn wata na di tɔŋ dɛn na di fɔs istri Tamil kɔntri — pat pan di ɛvride injinɛri fɔ wan bizi pɔt.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiyalur Ur: Wan poem bɔt di Tɛn Idylls we Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar rayt, we de prez di Chola kiŋ Karikal Valavan ɛn in pɔt siti we gɛt bɔku bɔku pipul dɛn we nem Kaveripoompattinam (Puhar), wit in ship dɛn, makit dɛn, ɛn fɛstival dɛn.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Nakkeerar. D: Wan poem fɔ di Tɛn Idylls we Nakkeerar rayt. Insay di lɔng ɛn kol briz we kin blo na di nɔt insay di kol sizin, wan kwin kin want in man we di kiŋ de kia fɔ in sojaman dɛn we wund na wan wɔ kamp.
A portrait coin of the Chera king Kuttuv: Wan pikchɔ kɔyn fɔ di Chera kiŋ Kuttuvan Kotai, we dɛn gi am in nem insay Tamil-Brahmi. Wit di Makkotai kɔyn dɛm, dɛn silva ishu dɛm ya we nɔ bɔku — sɔntɛm dɛn inspɛkt dɛn frɔm di Roman pɔtrɛt kɔyn dɛm we de kam tru tred — na wan pan di fɔs Indian kɔyn dɛm fɔ sho wan rula in fes.
A potsherd inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi, fo: Wan pɔt we dɛn rayt insay Tamil-Brahmi, we dɛn fɛn na Tissamaharama na di sawt pat na Sri Lanka ɛn we dɛn rayt arawnd di ia 200 bifo Krays. We dɛn rayt insay Tamil bɔt pɔt we de fa frɔm di Tamil men land, i sho se Tamil biznɛsman dɛn bin de wok akɔdin to di si insay di fɔstɛm istri tɛm.
A rare book from the first decades of Ta: Wan buk we nɔ bɔku frɔm di fɔs dikɛd ia dɛn we dɛn bin de print Tamil, we dɛn bin de sɛt di klas tɛks dɛn we dɛn bin kip pan pam lif dɛn fɔ di fɔs tɛm.
A rare volume digitised from CICT’s arch: Wan rare volyum we dɛn dijitayz frɔm CICT’s archive ɛn kip am fɔ stɔdi. Di wan dɛn we de kia fɔ di myuziɔm go ad ful ditil dɛn bɔt di katalog.
A Sangam-age Chola coin with a tiger and: Wan Sangam-ej Chola kɔyn we gɛt tayga ɛn ɛlifant. Fɔs Chola kɔyn dɛn, bɔku pan dɛn na kɔpa, de sɛnt pan di tayga — di sem emblem we di impyɔrial Chola dɛn go kɛr wan tawzin ia afta dat. Uraiyur ɛn Kaveripoompattinam na bin dɛn big big sɛnta dɛn.
A Sangam-age Pandya coin, typically a sm: Wan Sangam-ej Pandya kɔyn, we dɛn kin kɔl smɔl skwea we dɛn mek wit kɔpa we gɛt ɛlifant na wan say ɛn fish we dɛn mek wit stayl na di ɔda say. Dɛn kayn kɔyn dɛn de bin de skata insay ɛn rawnd Madurai, we na di Pandya kapital siti we dɛn bin de sɛlibret na Maduraikkanchi.
A scholarly study of government, adminis: Wan stɔdi we masta sabi bukman dɛn bin du bɔt gɔvmɛnt, administreshɔn, ɛn soshal layf na di Tamil kɔntri we bin de insay di Sangam tɛm.
A second coin of the Kongu Cheras. Compa: Wan sɛkɔn kɔyn we di Kongu Cheras dɛn mek. Kɔmpia di tu: kɔyn dɛn we dɛn kin slap wit an kin difrɛn pan strayk, wear ɛn kɔt, ɛn dɛn kayn difrɛns ya kin ɛp di wan dɛn we sabi bɔt mɔni biznɛs fɔ sɔlv di prɔblɛm dɛn ɛn tray fɔ no aw lɔng kɔyn dɛn bin de na di say we dɛn de yuz.
A second image of the four-armed, seated: Wan sɛkɔn imej fɔ di Ganesha we gɛt 4 an ɛn we sidɔm. Kɔmpia in prɔpɔshɔn, ɔnamɛnt ɛn di tɔn we di trɔnk tɔn wit di fɔs wan: insay di shered kanɔn fɔ di Silpa Sastras, ɛvri skapul ɛn wokshɔp lɛf in yon tɔch.
A selection drawn from the Thirukkural,: Wan sɛlɛkshɔn we dɛn pul frɔm di Thirukkural, we gɛda kɔplet dɛn we pɔsin go mɛmba fɔ di wan dɛn we de rid.
A separate photographing of the opening: Wan sɛpret foto fɔ di opin lif dɛn na bɔndɛl 579 D, di Maduraikkanchi.
Wan Shaiva sent, an dɛn jɔyn fɔ wɔship. Di Chola kiŋ dɛn bin ɔnɔ di siksti tri Nayanmar dɛn, we Sekkizhar bin tɔk bɔt dɛn layf insay di Periya Puranam, ɛn dɛn bin de mek dɛn brɔnz imej dɛn na tɛmpul dɛn ɛn kɛr dɛn go na fɛstival prushɔn dɛn.
A sherd illustrated in Vimala Begley’s 1: Wan sherd we dɛn sho na Vimala Begley in 1983 stɔdi bɔt Arikamedu in detin. We i bin de chɛk bak di layers we dɛn bin dig, Begley bin agyu se di siti bin bigin arawnd di mid-tɛd sɛntiwɔd bifo Krays — bifo tɛm pas aw Mɔtima Wila bin dɔn prɔpos — wit di Mɛditarenian kɔntakt dɛn bay di let sɛkɔn sɛntiwɔd bifo Krays. Di de dɛn we i bin rayt stil na tin we masta sabi bukman dɛn ɛksplen.
A sherd of an urn found in 2004, decorat: Wan shed pan wan urn we dɛn fɛn insay 2004, we dɛn dekɔret wit aplai rilif wit wan uman figa we tinap bitwin motif dɛn we dɛn kin rid as padi stɔl, wan dia, kren ɛn krokodail. Masta sabi bukman dɛn dɔn si insay am wan fɔs mama gɔd — sɔm, as di fim se, wan fɔs pɔsin fɔ Kotravai, di wɔ gɔd uman fɔ Sangam poem. Na wan pan di fichural pikchɔ dɛn we nɔ bɔku na Ayɔn Ij Tamil Nadu.
A short illustrated guide for visitors:: Wan shɔt gayd we gɛt pikchɔ fɔ di wan dɛn we de kam fɔ si di ples: wetin na di Sangam poem dɛn, aw dɛn grup dɛn, ɛn aw akam ɛn puram poem dɛn ɛn di fayv land skay dɛn de wok.
A silver kasu of Rajendra Chola combinin: Wan silva kasu fɔ Rajendra Chola we de kɔba royal emblems — di Chola tayga wit di Pandya fish ɛn Chera bo. Adichanallur did not stand alone. Along: Adichanallur nɔ bin tinap in wan. Di vali bin gɛt ayɛn, kɔpa ɛn gold fɔ wok, fayn fayn rays land, ɛn riva rod we de go na di si. Urn bɛrin dɛm we gɛt di sem tradishɔn de ɔlsay na di Galf na Sri Lanka, ɛn bidz dɛm we dɛn mek wit ston dɛm we de fa bin rich na di vali — fɔs sayn dɛm fɔ di chenj we go mek di Tamil kɔst bi wan hab fɔ Indian Oshɔn tred insay sɔm ɔndrɛd ia. Agriculture remains an important part of: Agrikalchɔral biznɛs stil impɔtant pan Tamil Nadu in ikɔmi ɛn rural layf. Di men tin dɛn we dɛn kin plant na rays, shugaken, kɔtɔn, grɔnnat, puls, ɛn malet, ɛn di we aw dɛn kin plant dɛn kin difrɛn akɔdin to di grɔn, ren, wata we dɛn kin plant, ɛn di tin dɛn we di makit want. Di fama dɛm tide de yuz wan kɔmbaynshɔn fɔ tradishɔnal no ɛn kɔntempɔral tɛknɔlɔji dɛm, lɛk trakta, mɛkanikal avɛsta, impɔtant sid dɛm, irigashɔn pɔmp, ɛn di we aw dɛn de manej di grɔn. Drip irigashɔn ɛn ɔda we dɛn we nɔ de yuz wata fayn kin ɛp fɔ manej di wata we nɔ bɔku na fayn fam sistɛm dɛn. Fama dɛn kin gɛt prɔblɛm dɛn bak lɛk ren we nɔ kin kam ɔltɛm, dray sizin, di kɔst fɔ input we de go ɔp, di shɔt we aw dɛn de wok, ɛn di prayz we de chenj na di makit. So di agrikalchɔral ɛritij na Tamil Nadu ripresent ɔl tu wan lɔng istri fɔ adap to lokal envayrɔmɛnt kɔndishɔn ɛn wan sɛktɔ we de chenj we de ansa to di mɔdan ikɔmik ɛn klaymat prɛshɔn.
Agriculture was an important source of f: Agrikalchɔral biznɛs na bin impɔtant tin fɔ it, fɔ liv, ɛn fɔ gɛt mɔni na di Tamil pipul dɛn we bin de trade trade. Sangam buk dɛn, we dɛn kin tɔk bɔt di tɛm we bin de arawnd 300 B.C.E.–300 C.E., de tɔk bɔt di kɔmyuniti dɛn we dɛn bin de du fam wok, di fil dɛn we dɛn bin de plant, di ren we bin de kam insay di sizin, di layfstɔk, ɛn di wok we dɛn bin de du fɔ wok na fam. Tamil poet dɛn bin kɔnɛkt difrɛn land skay dɛn wit difrɛn we dɛn fɔ liv. Di Marutham land skay bin ripresent fayn fayn agrikalchɔral land dɛn, usay dɛn bin de plant padi ɛn ɔda fam wok dɛn we dɛn bin de du bin impɔtant. Di fama dɛn bin de pik di tin dɛn we dɛn kin plant akɔdin to di we aw di grɔn de, di ren we kin kam, ɛn di wata we de. Rays, malet, shugaken, puls, kɔtɔn, ɛn sɛsam na sɔm pan di tin dɛn we dɛn bin tɔk bɔt we dɛn bin de stɔdi bɔt aw dɛn bin de plant Tamil trade trade. Fam bin dipen pan mɔtalman wok, animal pawa, ɛn no bɔt di lokal envayrɔmɛnt kɔndishɔn. Literature pruf de gi valyu tin fɔ no bɔt agrikalchɔral layf, pan ɔl we dɛn fɔ ɛksplen am nia akiɔlɔjik ɛn istri risach.

An animated reconstruction of the ancien: Wan animated rikostrɔkshɔn fɔ di ol we, frɔm di dokyumɛnti bɔt Kallanai we di Sɛntral Instityut fɔ Klasik Tamil bin mek. Di tim dɛn we de wok ɛn ɛlifant dɛn bin de pul big big ston dɛn go na di riva ɛn drɔp dɛn na di riva. As di kɔrɛnt bin de skata di san we bin de ɔnda dɛn, dɛn bin de sink, ɛn dɛn bin gɛda mɔ ston dɛn pan tap te di hip rɛst pan strɔng grɔn. Dɔn kle ɛn di silt we di wata bin de rɔn bin ful-ɔp di say dɛn we nɔ bin de, ɛn dɛn bin tay di rɔk dɛn fɔ mek dɛn bi wan natura l tin we nɔ go mek wata pas.
An archaeologist cleans the shoulder of: Wan man we de stɔdi bɔt aw pipul dɛn bin de du tin trade trade, de klin di sholda fɔ wan big bɔks we de na di rɛd grɔn we de na di mawnten usay dɛn bɛr pipul dɛn. Di wan dɛn we bin de dig insay 2004 bin fɛn urn dɛn we ay lɛk tri fit — nia wan mita —, we big fɔ gɛt di bɔdi we lɛf pan di wan dɛn we dɔn day. Vesel dɛn we gɛt dis saiz bin de kɔl fɔ rial skil: wan Sangam poet adrɛs di pɔsin we de mek urn as கலம்செய் கோவே, “O kiŋ bitwin pɔt dɛn”.

An excavated settlement near the Vaigai: Wan siti we dɛn dig nia di Vaigai na Sivaganga distrikt, wit brik strɔkchɔ, pɔt ɛn bɔku tin dɛn we dɛn mek.
An excavator lifts a small pot from insi: Wan pɔsin we de dig kin es wan smɔl pɔt frɔm insay wan big bɛrin urn. Dɛn bin de put pɔt, bol ɛn lid insay ɛn rawnd di urn dɛn wit di wan dɛn we dɔn day, sɔntɛm dɛn bin de ol it, wata ɔ ɔfrin — wan sayn we de sho se di pipul dɛn na Adichanallur bin de imajin wan waka we pas day. Insay di fim wan ɛlda ɛksplen se dɛn bin gi di wan dɛn we dɔn day tin dɛn fɔ ɛp dɛn we dɛn de go: “na dat min di urn”.
An institution of the Ministry of Educat: Wan institiushɔn fɔ di Ministri fɔ Edukeshɔn, Gɔvmɛnt fɔ India, na Chennai, we de fɔ di stɔdi ɛn prɔmoshɔn fɔ Klasik Tamil — di langwej fɔ di fɔti wan ol wok dɛn, frɔm Tolkappiyam to Muttollayiram.
An iron blade and a knife, measured agai: Wan ayɛn bled ɛn wan nɛf, we dɛn mɛzhɔ wit skel. An old Tanjore painting of Rama’s corona: Wan ol Tanjore peint fɔ Rama in korona. Rama we gɛt grɛn skin sidɔm na tron ​​wit Sita, in brɔda dɛn de atɛnd wit flay-whisk ɛn parasol, Hanuman de na in fut, ɛn sɛj ɛn vanaras dɛn de krawd di kɔt. Klosap ɔl di say dɛn we dɛn de, dɛn dɔn gild wit gold ɛn put ston dɛn; di we aw dɛn wɛr di gold ɛn di pent de sho aw i dɔn ol ɛn aw dɛn dɔn yuz am fɔ lɔng tɛm fɔ wɔship.
An urn exposed in a trench at Sivakalai,: Wan urn we dɛn sho na wan trench na Sivakalai, we de lɛk sɛvin kilomita frɔm Adichanallur along di Thamirabarani. Di Tamil Nadu Stet Dipatmɛnt fɔ Akiɔlɔji bin dig Sivakalai frɔm 2019, ɛn dɛn dɔn gi urn dɛn we gɛt padi ɛn ayɛn tin dɛn, ɛn wan ples usay pipul dɛn de liv nia de; di dipatmɛnt dɔn ripɔt di redio kabon deti fɔ in padi we rich bak to di twɛlv sɛntiwɔd bifo Krays. Tugeda di tu sayt dɛn de sho wan bizi Ayɔn Ij land skay nia di riva.
Ancient and medieval Tamil irrigation sy: Di Tamil irigashɔn sistem dɛn we bin de trade ɛn insay di midul ivul bin de yuz say dɛn we dɛn bin tek tɛm mek fɔ kɔntrol aw wata de kɔmɔt na tank dɛn ɛn go na agrikalchɔral chanɛl dɛn. Dɛn strɔkchɔ dɛn ya nɔ bin jɔs bi say dɛn we dɛn kin opin na wan tank wɔl; difrɛn dizayn dɛn bin ɛp fɔ rigul di wata we de flɔ ɛn sheb di wata we dɛn dɔn kip to fil dɛm. Bɔku tradishɔnal sluis tayp dɛn de we dɛn rayt na Tamil Nadu, lɛk madai, madagu, thumpu ɛn kumizhi. Di rayt we aw dɛn bin mek dɛn ɛn di wok we dɛn bin de du bin difrɛn. Wan ɛgzampul we rili intrestin na di kumizhi sistem, we na spɛshal sluis we gɛt fɔ du wit tradishɔnal tank-wata manejmɛnt. Sluys bin de ɛp fama dɛn fɔ fri wata we dɛn nid am, pas fɔ alaw di tank fɔ ɛmti we dɛn nɔ ebul fɔ kɔntrol am, ɛn dɛn bin de sɔpɔt fɔ ɔganayz fɔ sheb wata tru chanɛl dɛn we de sav difrɛn agrikalchɔral eria dɛn. Dɛn kɔnstrɔkshɔn de sho prɛktikal no bɔt wata prɛshɔn, ɔlt ples, graviti ɛn di rilayshɔn bitwin stɔrɔj ​​tank ɛn fam land. Di tin dɛn we dɛn rayt we stil de alayv na impɔtant pruf fɔ dis irigashɔn tɛknɔlɔji ɛn di wok we i de du fɔ chenj di agrikalchɔral land skay.

In classical Tamil literature the five t: Insay klasical Tamil litrɛcha di fayv tinai land skay dɛm — Kurinji, Mullai, Marutham, Neithal ɛn Palai — nɔto jɔs di jiografi bɔt dɛn de tɔk bak bɔt pipul dɛn wok, natura risɔs, imɔshɔn ɛn we fɔ liv. In Perundurai taluk, Erode district, Kod: Insay Perundurai taluk, Erode distrikt, Kodumanal sho di prodakshɔn sayd fɔ tred. In Ramanathapuram district, near the Vai: Insay Ramanathapuram distrikt, nia di Vaigai ɛn lɛk tri kilomita frɔm di shore tide, Alagankulam na wan impɔtant say fɔ trade trade na di sawt-ist kɔst. In the far south, the early Pandyas of M: Insay di fa sawt, di fɔs Pandya dɛn na Madurai (7th–10th sɛntiwɔd) bin hol di say dɛn we dɛn de wɔship frɔm granit il dɛn, lɛk na Thirupparankundram, ɛn na Kalugumalai dɛn bin kɔt di Vettuvan Koil — wan ɔl tɛmpul we dɛn kɔt dɔŋ frɔm wan rɔk, we dɛn nɔ dɔn — nia row dɛn we gɛt fayn fayn Jain figa dɛn we dɛn kɔt. In the first centuries CE, Roman ships r: Insay di fɔstɛm Kristian dɛn tɛm, di Roman ship dɛn bin de rayd di monsɔn briz fɔ go na di Tamil kɔst fɔ pepa, pal, gem ɛn fayn klos, ɛn dɛn bin de pe wit gold ɛn silva. In the most famous passage of the Sittan: Insay di say we pipul dɛn sabi pas ɔl na di Sittanavasal siling, wan yɔŋ man we gɛt kɔl ia, i ol wan lotus we wan ɔda wan de waka nia am, wan bɔfa we ayd af-af bitwin di big big rɛd bɔd dɛn. In the warm, humid Tamil country a palm: Insay di Tamil kɔntri we wam ɛn wet, wan pam lif kin las fɔ sɔm ɔndrɛd ia pas ɔl; insekt, wet ɛn aw fɔ ol am kin west am. On the Amaravathi river, Karur — remembe: Na di Amaravathi riva, Karur — we dɛn mɛmba as Vanchi ɛn Karuvur — na bin wan inland sɛnta we gɛt fɔ du wit di Chera kiŋ dɛn. Di Tamil Nadu Dipatmɛnt fɔ Akiɔlɔji ripɔt se pɔt dɛn we dɛn rayt insay Tamil-Brahmi, Roman amphora fragmɛnt dɛn, rouletteted ware, Roman ɛn ɔda kɔyn dɛn, valyu ston dɛn, bidz dɛn ɛn brik strɔkchɔ dɛn. Karur bin de na rod dɛn we go dɔn mek di wɛst ɛn ist kɔst, go na Muziris ɛn Arikamedu; in Roman kɔyn dɛn de sho se dɛn gɛt mɔni, bɔt nɔto fɔ se na dairekt tred wit Rom.
On the banks of the Thamirabarani in Tho: Na di bank dɛn na di Thamirabarani na Thoothukudi distrikt, wan pan di big big ples dɛn fɔ bɛr pipul dɛn na India we dɛn kɔl Ayɔn Ij. Fɔs dig insay 1876 ɛn Alɛgzanda Ria bin dig am bitwin 1899 ɛn 1905, ɛn bak bay di Akiɔlɔjik Sɔv fɔ India frɔm 2004, Adichanallur dɔn gɛt big big ɔn dɛn we gɛt mɔtalman bɔdi, we dɛn le wit ayɛn tul ɛn wɛpɔn, brɔnz bɔtul, ɔnamɛnt ɛn gold mɔt-band. Sangam poems already speak of painters a: Sangam poem dɛn dɔn ɔlrɛdi tɔk bɔt peint ɛn hal dɛn we dɛn dɔn peint: di ஓவியர் we bin de drɔ wit fayn fayn layn dɛn, ɛn di ஓவியச் செந்நூல், di triti bɔt peint. Wetin de alayv pan wɔl bigin insay di 7th–9th sɛntiwɔd — na Pallava tɛmpul dɛm ɛn di Jain kev na Sittanavasal — ɛn i de rɔn tru di big Chola fresko dɛm na Thanjavur to di brayt Nayak mural dɛm ɛn di gilded Tanjore panɛl dɛm fɔ di 17th–19th sɛntiwɔd. Minral ɛn plant kɔlɔ dɛn — rɛd ɛn yɔlɔ ɔk, lamp-blak, laym wayt, grɛn grɔn — dɛn bin de le dɛn pan laym plasta insay wan tradishɔn we bin las fɔ pas wan tawzin ia.
Sangam poems are classed as akam (the in: Dɛn kin put Sangam poem dɛn as akam (di insay wɔl fɔ lɔv) ɔ puram (di ɔda wɔl fɔ wɔ, kiŋship, fri-an, ɛn ɛtiks). Akam poem dɛn nɔ de ɛva gi nem to di wan dɛn we dɛn lɛk; dɛn de tɔk tru tayp dɛn — di hiroin, di hiro, di padi, di fosta-mama.

Tamil farmers traditionally cultivated c: Frɔm trade trade, di Tamil fama dɛn bin de plant tin dɛn we fit fɔ difrɛn grɔn, di we aw ren kin kam, ɛn di wata we dɛn kin gɛt. Padi bin impɔtant mɔ na say dɛn we gɛt fayn fayn wata, we malet lɛk kambu ɛn varagu bin fayn fɔ difrɛn agrikalchɔral say dɛn we dray. Pul, sɛsam, kɔtɔn, shuga, ɛn ɔda tin dɛn bak bin de pat pan di rijinal faming sistɛm dɛn. Di agrikalchɔral wok dɛn bin de fala di sizin kɔndishɔn: di fama dɛn bin de pripia fil, pik sid, plant krop, manej wata, pul gras, ɛn avɛst akɔdin to wetin ɛni krop nid. Fɔ no bɔt ren, di fayn fayn tin dɛn we di grɔn kin gɛt, ɛn di chenj dɛn we kin apin insay di sizin bin rili impɔtant fɔ plan aw fɔ plant. Difrɛn rijyɔn dɛn bin mek dɛn yon krop kɔmbaynshɔn ɛn agrikalchɔral kalenda. Istri stɔdi dɛm pan Sangam litrechɔ sho se di ol Tamil fama dɛm bin ɔndastand di impɔtant tin fɔ pik fayn krop ɛn adap di we aw dɛn de plant am to di lokal envayrɔmɛnt kɔndishɔn.

Tamil literature describes fine garments: Tamil buk dɛn de tɔk bɔt fayn fayn klos dɛn, kɔtɔn tɛkstayl dɛn, pipul dɛn we sabi wok wit tɛkstayl ɛn tred. Porunaratrupadai kɔmpia fayn fayn klos to tin dɛn we rili fayn; Dɛn kɔl Purananuru fɔ nilikachchai, we na wan klos we gɛt fɔ du wit indigo kɔlɔ. Tamil poetics gives each mood of love a: Tamil poetiks de gi ɛni mud fɔ lɔv wan land skay. Di Tolkappiyam nem di land (nilam) ɛn di tɛm (pozhuthu) fɔ ɛni tinai as in fɔs ɛlimɛnt dɛn (mutharporul), in gɔd dɛn, pipul dɛn, it, bɔd dɛn, flawa dɛn ɛn myuzik as in yon ɛlimɛnt dɛn (karupporul), ɛn di faz fɔ lɔv we i de kɛr as in tim (uripporul). Wan flawa ɔ bɔd we de na Sangam poem na inf fɔ sɛt di wan ol tin — ɛn di pɔsin we de lisin kin no wan tɛm if di wan dɛn we lɛk dɛnsɛf mit, wet, agyu, pain ɔ pat.
Tamil seafarers sailed with the monsoon: Tamil pipul dɛn we de wok na di si bin de travul wit di monsɔn briz we bin de blo bifo di kɔmɔn tɛm. Sangam poem dɛn de tɔk bɔt di ship dɛn (kalam) we di Yavana dɛn bin de kam na Muziris we ful-ɔp wit gold ɛn we de kɔmɔt wit pepa, ɛn di Pattinappalai de pikchɔ di bizi haba na Kaveripattinam (Puhar). Ɔnda di Cholas, bot dɛn bin de krɔs di Bay of Bengal: dɛn rayt di tin dɛn we Rajendra I bin go fɛt Srivijaya, arawnd di ia 1025 afta Krays. No ol Tamil hul nɔ de alayv ɔl, so dis mɔdel na wan atis in intapriteshɔn, nɔto di rikostrɔkshɔn fɔ wan bot we dɛn sabi.
Tamil tradition remembers seven chieftai: Tamil tradishɔn mɛmba sɛvin chif dɛn na di Sangam ej pas ɔl ɔda wan dɛn fɔ di giv-ɔp: Pari, Pegan, Kari, Ay Andiran, Adhiyaman, Nalli ɛn Ori. List ɛn di ditel dɛn difrɛn bitwin akɔdin dɛn, bɔt togɛda dɛn de ɛmbodi kodai — fri-an — as di mak fɔ wan rula we fit. Di poet dɛn we dɛn bin de sɔpɔt bin de sɛlibret dɛn gift dɛn insay vas, ɛn so di poem dɛn bin kip dɛn nem dɛn layf.
Tamil-Brahmi cave records, Chola temple: Tamil-Brahmi kev rɛkɔd dɛn, Chola tɛmpul inskripshɔn dɛn, ɛn kiŋ in kɔpa-plet grant dɛn.
Tamil-Brahmi is the script of the earlie: Tamil-Brahmi na di skript fɔ di fɔs Tamil inskripshɔn dɛn we dɛn sabi. Bɔku pan dɛn na shɔt donativ rɛkɔd dɛn we dɛn kɔt pan di drip-lɛj ɛn ston bed dɛn na di natura cavern dɛn we dɛn gi to ascetics.

Teams of workers and elephants drag grea: Tim dɛn we de wok ɛn ɛlifant dɛn de drɛg big big ston dɛn to di Kaveri insay dis rikostrɔkshɔn frɔm di fim. Dɛn nɔ bin de yuz ɛni mɔta na Kallanai: di trɛnk we di dɛm gɛt bin de pan di saiz ɛn wet we in ston dɛn we dɛn nɔ kɔt bin gɛt. Fɔ muv dɛn bay mɔsul nɔmɔ na bin big big tin we dɛn bin de du fɔ ɔganayz, ɛn di Tamil tradishɔn se na bikɔs di Chola kiŋ Karikalan bin want am.
Ten decads of puram poems in praise of t: Tɛn dikɛd puram poem dɛn fɔ prez di Chera kiŋ dɛn, ɛn ɛni wan pan dɛn dekad pan wan kiŋ; di fɔs ɛn las dikɛd ia dɛn kin lɔs.
Tens of thousands of Tamil palm-leaf man: Tɛn tawzin Tamil pam-lif manuskrip dɛn — buk ɛn grama, tɛmpul ritual, Siddha mɛrɛsin, astronomi, astrɔlɔji, myuzik ɛn akɔdin — dɛn kin kip na pɔblik kɔleshiɔn. Thanjavur became a major centre of power: Thanjavur bin bi wan men sɛnta fɔ pawa insay di Chola tɛm. Ɔnda Rajaraja Chola I, di siti bin si we dɛn bin de bil di fayn fayn Brihadisvara Tɛmpl, we dɛn bin dɔn fɔ bil insay di fɔs pat pan di ia 1900. Di tɛmpul de sho di tin dɛn we di Cholas dɛn dɔn du pan akitɛkɛt, injinɛri, skapul, rilijɔn sɔpɔt ɛn administreshɔn. Di tin dɛn we dɛn rayt na di tɛmpul wɔl dɛn de gi valyu tin dɛn bɔt doneshɔn, di we aw dɛn de manej di tɛmpul, di wan dɛn we de wok ɛn di tin dɛn we dɛn de du fɔ mek mɔni. The agal vilakku was a small lamp, commo: Di agal vilakku na bin smɔl lamp, we dɛn kin yuz kle ɔ mɛtal, we dɛn kin yuz fɔ mek layt insay os dɛn. I bin gɛt ɔyl ɛn wik, we dɛn bin de layt fɔ mek faya kɔmɔt. Dɛn bin de yuz ɔyl lamp fɔ ɔdinari layt na os ɛn dɛn bin de ple bak pan rilijɔn sɛrimɔni dɛn ɛn tradishɔnal sɛrimɔni dɛn. Di simpul we aw dɛn mek dɛn bin mek dɛn bi tin dɛn we pɔsin kin yuz na os.
The ammi was a traditional stone tool us: Di ammi na bin tradishɔnal ston tul we dɛn bin de yuz fɔ grind spays, chili, kokonat ɛn ɔda tin dɛn. Dɛn bin de put di tin dɛn we dɛn go yuz fɔ mek di it pan di flat ston ɛn rɔb dɛn wit smɔl anston te dɛn bi paste. I bin yusful mɔ fɔ pripia chutney, spays miksɔp ɛn kuk paste. Di ammi stil bi wan simbul we pipul sabi fo tradishonal Tamil kuk.
The ancient port of Arikamedu near Puduc: Di ol pɔt na Arikamedu nia Puducherry bin gɛt Roman amphora, Arretine pɔt, ɛn glas, we sho se di tred bitwin di Tamil kɔst ɛn di Roman wɔl bin de ɔltɛm ɛn bɔku.
The Arani silk saree originates from Ara: Di Arani silk saree kɔmɔt frɔm Arani we de na Tiruvannamalai distrikt, Tamil Nadu, we na wan rijyɔn we pipul dɛn sabi fɔ in silk-wevin industri. Trade trade, dɛn kin mek dɛn saree ya wit silk yarn, ɛn dɛn kin gɛt bɔku bɔku kɔlɔ dɛn, pɔtn dɛn, ɛn bɔda stayl dɛn. Dɛn dizayn dɛn de frɔm tradishɔnal pɔtn dɛn we nɔ rili simpul to saree dɛn we dɛn dɔn dɛkɔret fayn fayn wan we dɛn mek fɔ fɛstival ɛn sɛrimɔni. Arani in wef ɛritij dipen pan spɛshal no bɔt aw fɔ pripia di yan, aw fɔ yuz di loom, aw fɔ kɔba di kɔlɔ, ɛn aw fɔ dɔn di klos. Wivin dɔn sɔpɔt lokal layf ɛn i dɔn ɛp fɔ mek di rijyɔn in tɛkstayl ikɔmi fɔ lɔng lɔng tɛm. Pan ɔl we wi nɔ shɔ di rayt ia we dɛn bigin fɔ mek silk we dɛn kɔl Arani, di tradishɔn stil bi impɔtant pat pan di tin dɛn we dɛn de mek wit an na Tamil Nadu. The Buddha with his hand raised in abhay: Di Buddha wit in an we i es ɔp insay abhaya mudra, di jes we se “nɔ fred”. Budis bin bɔku na di Chola tɛm Nagapattinam, usay Rajaraja I bin gi wan monasti fɔ di kiŋ na Srivijaya, ɛn dɛn bin mek bɔku bɔku Budist brɔnz dɛn di we aw dɛn bin de mek Chola.
The cabinets in this wing hold CICT edit: Di kabinɛt dɛn we de na dis wing gɛt CICT ɛdyushɔn dɛn fɔ di Tɛn Idylls ɛn di Eight Anthologies. Opin wan glas domɔt, pik wan volyum, ɛn tɔn in pej dɛn na di rida. Yu kin dawnlod ɛni volyum bak fɔ stɔdi.
The capital Rajendra I founded to commem: Di kapital siti we nem Rajendra I bin bil fɔ mɛmba in kampen na di nɔt; in big Shiva tɛmpul stil de, bɔku pan di siti nɔ de.
The cave inscriptions at Mangulam near M: Di tin dɛn we dɛn rayt na di kev na Mangulam nia Madurai na wan pan di ol wan dɛn we dɛn rayt bɔt Tamil-Brahmi. Dɛn kin tɔk bɔt di Pandya rula we nem Nedunchezhiyan ɛn di gift dɛn we dɛn kin gi mɔnk dɛn.
The celebrated early Chola king of Patti: Di sɛlibret fɔs Chola kiŋ na Pattinappalai ɛn Porunaratruppadai, we win di fɛt na Venni insay di buk dɛn we dɛn rayt. Tradishɔn se na Kallanai, di ol divɛshɔn weir akɔdin to di Kaveri we bin de wata di dɛlta; di strɔkchɔ dɔn ripɛnt ɛn chenj fɔ lɔng lɔng tɛm.
The Chera capital of Sangam poetry and S: Di Chera kapital fɔ Sangam poem ɛn Silappathikaram. Dɛn de agyu bɔt usay i bin tinap: bɔku pipul dɛn we de rayt bɔt istri se na Karur na Tamil Nadu, ɔda wan dɛn se na Thiruvanchikulam nia Kodungallur na Kerala. Dɛn tu kandidet ya gɛt mak, dash.
The Chera, Chola, and Pandya dynasties e: Di Chera, Chola, ɛn Pandya famili dɛn ɔl bin de gi kɔyn dɛn we gɛt dɛn kiŋ in mak dɛn: di bɔ (Chera), di tayga (Chola), ɛn di fish (Pandya). Bɔku pan di fɔstɛm Tamil kɔyn dɛn, dɛn bin de kɔt dɛn wit kɔpa, ɛn sɔm na silva ɛn lid.

The cultivated fields and river plains,: Di fil dɛn we dɛn kin plant ɛn di riva dɛn we nɔ gɛt bɛtɛ wata, we di ples kin shayn insay ɛvri sizin. In gɔd na Vendhan (Indra), ɛn in tik na di marutham. The earliest known Tamil writing, carved: Di fɔs Tamil raytin we dɛn sabi, we dɛn kɔt insay kev ɛn skrach pan pɔt, frɔm Mangulam, Jambai, Pugalur, ɛn Keezhadi.
The earliest Tamil dynastic coins, from: Di fɔstɛm Tamil dinastik kɔyn dɛn, frɔm arawnd di las ɔndrɛd ia bifo Krays, bɔku pan dɛn na smɔl smɔl skwea ɔ rawnd kɔpa ɛn lid. Pandya kɔyn dɛn kin pe wan ɛlifant wit wan fish we dɛn mek wit stayl; Chola kɔyn dɛn de sho tayga, bɔku tɛm i kin gɛt ɛlifant ɔ ɔs; Chera kɔyn dɛn gɛt di bɔw ɛn aro. Sɔm pipul dɛn kin kɔl di wan dɛn we dɛn gi dɛn insay Tamil-Brahmi, lɛk di Pandya kɔyn dɛn we de rid பெருவழுதி (Peruvazhuthi) ɛn di silva pikchɔ kɔyn dɛn we di Chera kiŋ dɛn Makkotai ɛn Kuttuvan Kotai bin mek. Dɛn dɔn fɛn bɔku pan dɛn na di bed na di Amaravathi riva na Karur, we na di ol Chera sɛnta.
The early Pandya port near the mouth of: Di fɔs Pandya pɔt nia di mawnten fɔ di Thamirabarani, we bin gɛt nem fɔ in pal fisha. Frɔm da tɛm de, di si dɔn go dɔŋ, ɛn i dɔn lɛf di vilej insay di land.
The eight-armed goddess, her face painte: Di gɔd uman we gɛt et an, we dɛn pent in fes blu, tinap oba di bɔfa dɛbul Mahisha in ed, i ol sɔd, bo, aro, diskɔs ɛn shild, we tu uman dɛn de atɛnd am wit flay-wisk. Insay Tamil tradishɔn i gɛt fɔ du wit Korravai, di wɔ gɔd we win di Sangam poem dɛn.
The eri system was a major part of tradi: Di eri sistɛm na bin wan men pat pan tradishɔnal wata manejmɛnt na Tamil Nadu. eri na atifishal irigashɔn tank we dɛn mek fɔ gɛda ɛn kip ren wata ɛn wata we de rɔn ɔp di grɔn. We di mɔnt bin de kam, wata bin de gɛda biɛn wan grɔn we dɛn mek wit dɔti. Dɔn dɛn kin fri am fɔ agrikalchɔral wok we ren nɔ kin kam dɔŋ. Dɛn tank dɛn ya bin valyu mɔ na say dɛn we nɔ gɛt pɔsin we dɛn kin abop pan fɔ go na riva dɛn we de gro ɔltɛm. Wata we dɛn bin de kip bin de sɔpɔt fɔ plant padi ɛn ɔda tin dɛn we dɛn bin de plant, ɛn di tank bed dɛn ɛn di land we bin de rawnd bin de pat pan di vilej in agrikalchɔral land skay. Insay sɔm rijyɔn dɛn, dɛn bin arenj di tank dɛn insay kɔnɛkt sikyud: ɔvaflɔ frɔm wan ɔpa tank kin muf go insay wan lɔwa tank, ɛp di kɔmyuniti dɛn fɔ yuz di sizin ren we kin kam akɔdin to wan big eria. Di eri nɔ bin jɔs tan lɛk wata-stɔrɔj. I bin de pat pan wan big vilej sistɛm we bin nid fɔ de silt ɔltɛm, ripɛnt ɛn kɔlektif manejmɛnt. We dɛn bin de kia fɔ di tank dɛn fayn fayn wan, dɛn bin de ɛp fɔ ridyus di wata we de lɔs tru di wata we de rɔn we dɛn nɔ bin de kɔntrol ɛn dɛn bin de mek di wata we de de fayn fayn wan we di ples dray.

The first of the Ten Idylls (Pattuppattu: Di fɔs wan pan di Tɛn Idylls (Pattuppattu), we Nakkeerar bin mek. Insay dis “gayd poem” wan devotee we Lɔd Murugan blɛs, dayrɛkt ɔda pɔsin we de luk fɔ am, i de tɔk bɔt in siks oli ples dɛn we i de, we na di Arupadai Veedu.

The foods that travelled with Tamil trad: Di it dɛm we bin de travul wit Tamil tred — blak pepa, jinja ɛn tumara we dɛn bin de fɛn akɔdin to di Indian Oshɔn, sɛsam ɔyl, pam jaggery ɛn ɔni, ɛn di rays we pipul dɛn we de na di si bin de tek fɔ chenj fɔ fish ɛn sɔl.
The four families of Tamil instruments:: Di 4 famili dɛn fɔ Tamil inschrumɛnt dɛn: ayd — di kiŋ in murasu, di parai, di thavil, udukkai ɛn pambai; briz — di nadaswaram ɛn di bambu flut; string dɛn — di yazh fɔ di Sangam bard dɛn ɛn di veenai dɛn; ɛn mɛtal — di thalam.
The Gangaikondacholeeswaram Temple and i: Di Gangaikondacholeeswaram Tɛmpl ɛn di say we dɛn de rawnd am tide, we yu si am frɔm di ɛj.

The Grand Anicut at work: water rushing: Di Grand Anicut de wok: wata de rɔsh tru in vents, oba in spilway ɛn go insay di chanɛl dɛn na di delta. Futej frɔm di dokyumɛnti bɔt Kallanai we di Sɛntral Instityut fɔ Klasik Tamil bin mek.
The great courtyard seen through the pal: Di big kɔt we yu kin si tru di big big kɔlɔn dɛn ɛn arch dɛn na di pales.

The heroine of Silappathikaram, who prov: Di heroin fɔ Silappathikaram, we pruv se in man Kovalan inosɛns bifo di Pandya kiŋ bay we i brok opin in anklet: in yon bin ol rubi, di kwin in pal dɛn. Wan literary figure pas wan rekod istri pɔsin, i bi wan simbul fɔ jɔstis — ɛn dɛn de wɔship am as Pattini ɛn Kannaki Amman na Tamil Nadu, Kerala ɛn Sri Lanka.
The image of Shiva as Nataraja, Lord of: Di imej fɔ Shiva as Nataraja, Lɔd fɔ di Dans, we de dans insay wan ring we gɛt faya, na di Chola brɔnz fɔm we dɛn kin sɛlibret pas ɔl. I de sho di kɔsmik saykl fɔ krieshɔn, kip, ɛn disɔlshɔn.
The Jambai inscription in Villupuram dis: Di Jambai inskripshɔn na Villupuram distrikt gi nem “Satiyaputo Atiyan Netuman Anci”, we kɔnɛkt di Atiyaman chif dɛn wit di Satiyaputa we dɛn tɔk bɔt na Ashoka in ɛdikt dɛn.

The Kailasanatha Temple, a Pallava-perio: Di Kailasanatha Tɛmpl, we na wan tɛmpul we dɛn mek wit ston insay Pallava tɛm, wit di smɔl smɔl say dɛn we dɛn de wɔship we de layn di say we dɛn de rawnd am.
The kalayam, the everyday Tamil clay pot: Di kalayam, di ɛvride Tamil kle pɔt. I rawnd bɔdi ɛn smɔl nɛk de mek wata kol ɛn izi fɔ kɛr, ɛn dɛn stil de trowe kalaayam na di pɔsin we de mek pɔt in wil ɛn faya am na vilej kiln dɛn — we na wan living link to di vessel dɛn we dɛn dig na Tamil sayt dɛn.
The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across th: Di Kallanai, ɔ Grand Anicut, we de krɔs di Kaveri — we dɛn kin se na di Chola kiŋ Karikala — dɛn bil am fɔ rigul ɛn divayt di riva in wata to chanɛl fɔ irigashɔn. I mek di Kaveri delta bi wan pan di big big land dɛn we dɛn kin plant rays na Tamil Nadu, ɛn i stil de sav in irigashɔn sistɛm tide. (Luk di Irrigeshɔn rum fɔ no mɔ bɔt Tamil wata injinɛri.)
The Kanchipuram silk saree is one of the: Di Kanchipuram silk saree na wan pan di tradishɔnal tɛkstayl dɛn we dɛn kin sɛlibret pas ɔl na Tamil Nadu. Dis saree kɔmɔt na Kanchipuram, we na wan istri say usay dɛn de mek wiv, ɛn pipul dɛn sabi am fɔ in rich silk klos, intrikɛt zari wok, difrɛn bɔda dɛn, ɛn fayn fayn pɔtn dɛn. Di tradishɔnal motif dɛn na tɛmpul tawa dɛn, pikɔk, mango, flawa dɛn, ɛn jɔyometrik dizayn dɛn. Dɛn kin yuz silk yan we dɛn mek di saree, wit gold ɔ silva kɔlɔ zari trɛd dɛn we de ad dɛkɔretiv richnɛs. Kanchipuram silk saree dɛn gɛt impɔtant ples na Tamil mared, rilijɔn sɛrimɔni, fɛstival, ɛn ɔda spɛshal tɛm dɛn. Di we aw dɛn de mek di klos nid fɔ gɛt bɔku sɛns, mɔ we dɛn de jɔyn di bɔdi, di bɔda, ɛn di pallu we dɛn de yuz tradishɔnal we fɔ mek di bɔdi intalɔk. Di kraft bin de divɛlɔp fɔ lɔng lɔng tɛm, ɛn di rayt ia we dɛn bigin fɔ mek am nɔ bin dɔn bi istri. Kancheepuram Silk bin gɛt Jiografik Indikɛshɔn (GI) rɛkɔgnishɔn insay 2005. Tide, di saree ripresent Tamil Nadu in tɛkstayl ɛritij, skilful krafmanship, ɛn di kɔntinyu fɔ liv fɔ tradishɔnal wef kɔmyuniti dɛn.
The Kandangi saree is a traditional cott: Di Kandangi saree na tradishɔnal kɔtɔn tɛkstayl we gɛt fɔ du wit di Chettinad rijɔn, mɔ di Karaikudi ɛn di eria dɛn we de nia de. Dɛn no am fɔ in bold chɛk, strɛp, kɔntrast bɔda, ɛn strɔng kɔlɔ dɛn, lɛk rɛd, mɔstad, ɔrɛnj, ɛn dɔti brawn. Frɔm trade trade, in kɔtɔn klos we bin strɔng bin fayn fɔ yuz ɔltɛm, ɛn dis bin de sho di prɛktikal tin dɛn we dɛn nid fɔ wɛr ɛvride. Kandangi wef ripresent di difrɛn aesthetic ɛn tɛkstayl no bɔt di Chettinad rijɔn. I patɛn ɛn di kɔmbaynshɔn we i gɛt de mek i difrɛn frɔm bɔku ɔda Sawt Indian saree tradishɔn dɛn. Di we aw dɛn kin mek di klos na fɔ pripia di yan, arenj di trɛd dɛn na di loom, wev di klos, ɛn dɔn di bɔda dɛn ɛn dɔn. Gɔvmɛnt hanlɔm matirial de diskraib di tradishɔn se i dɔn de fɔ pas 150 ia, pan ɔl we dɛn stil nɔ shɔ di prɛsis ia we dɛn bigin am. Kandangi sarees bin gɛt GI rɛkɔgnishɔn insay 2019, we ɛp fɔ no ɛn kip dɛn rijinal aydentiti ɛn tradishɔnal krafmanship.
The Kaveri in flood at the anicut: Di Kaveri in flod na di anicut
The Kaveri in spate below the Grand Anic: Di Kaveri in spate dɔŋ di Grand Anicut. Tamil poet dɛn bin prez di Chola kɔntri as di land fɔ di Kaveri, we in bounty nɔ ɛva fel; di Silappatikaram de sɛlibret am as land we gɛt padi we nɔ gɛt bɔda. Di anicut bin tɔn da bɔnti de to wan sistɛm we dɛn de manej, ɛn di dɛlta bin bi di rays bol na di Tamil kɔntri.
The Kaveri rushing through the vents: Di Kaveri dɛn de rɔsh tru di vent dɛn

The Koorainadu saree is associated with: Di Koorainadu saree gɛt fɔ du wit Koorainadu nia Mayiladuthurai na Tamil Nadu. I gɛt sɔntin fɔ du mɔ wit di tradishɔnal klos we dɛn kin wɛr fɔ mared ɛn di kɔlchɔ we di tin dɛn we dɛn kin yuz fɔ mek klos gɛt na di Tamil mared kɔstɔm dɛn. Tradishonal varieties inklud silk en silk-cotton fabrik, wit difrɛn dizayn ɛn matirial dɛn we dɛn yuz akɔdin to di patikyula stayl ɛn purpose. Di saree de sho di wok we klos we dɛn wev de du na impɔtant famili sɛrimɔni ɛn di transmishɔn fɔ tɛkstayl tradishɔn bitwin jɛnɛreshɔn dɛn. Di we aw i tan, di klos we i mek, ɛn di tin dɛn we i de drɛs kin difrɛn, so dɛn fɔ rayt wan wan ɛgzampul dɛn akɔdin to di rial kɔnstrɔkshɔn we dɛn mek pas fɔ tink se ɛvri Koorainadu saree de fala di sem dizayn. Di rayt ia we dis tradishɔn bigin, dɛn nɔ dɔn tinap tranga wan. Koorainadu sarees stil bi wan valyu sɔbjɛkt fɔ fɛn di rilayshɔn bitwin klos, rijinal aydentiti, krafmanship, ɛn sɛrimɔni layf na Tamil Nadu.
The Kovai Kora cotton saree is associate: Di Kovai Kora kɔtɔn saree gɛt fɔ du wit Kɔmbatɔ ɛn di rijyɔn we de rawnd am we de mek tɛkstayl. Dɛn mek am wit kɔtɔn, ɛn pipul dɛn kin gladi fɔ in fayn fayn tin dɛn we nɔ fayn, di we aw i kin mek fayn, ɛn di bɔda dɛn we dɛn kin yuz trade trade. We yu kɔmpia am wit silk saree dɛn we dɛn dɔn ɔnamɛnt bad bad wan, bɔku tɛm, di Kɔra kɔtɔn tɛkstayl dɛn kin tɔk mɔ bɔt di we aw kɔtɔn kin tan lɛk aw i kin tan, di we aw i kin wɛr am fayn fayn wan, ɛn di difrɛn difrɛn tin dɛn we dɛn kin mek. Di saree de sho di impɔtant tin fɔ plant kɔtɔn, fɔ mek yan, fɔ wiv, ɛn fɔ sɛl tin dɛn fɔ mek klos na Tamil Nadu. Fɔ mek wan saree we dɛn mek wit an, yu nid fɔ tek tɛm pripia di wɔp ɛn weft trɛd dɛn ɛn yu nid fɔ yuz di loom fayn fayn wan. Kora kɔtɔn fayn fɔ difrɛn tɛm dɛn, lɛk fɔ wɛr ɛvride ɛn fɔ gɛda fɔmal wan dɛn. Kovai Kora Cotton bin gɛt GI rɛkɔgnishɔn insay 2008. Dɛn nɔ dɔn establish in ɛksaktɔl ia fɔdɔm, bɔt di tradishɔn stil bi impɔtant ɛgzampul fɔ di stet in difrɛn kɔtɔn-wev ɛritij.
The larger digitisation catalogued under: Di big dijitayzeshɔn we dɛn katalog ɔnda di sem nɔmba, 603 D: pas siks ɔndrɛd lif imej dɛn fɔ di bɔndɛl we dɛn kip di Kar Narpathu insay.
The last leaf of the bundle: Di las lif na di bɔndɛl
The Leiden plates record a Chola grant o: Di Leiden plet dɛn rayt wan Chola grant fɔ wan vilej to wan Budist vihara na Nagapattinam, we Rajaraja I bin ɔda ɛn we dɛn gi ɔnda Rajendra I. Naw dɛn kip dɛn na Leiden, insay di Netherlands.
The literary image of ancient Tamil mari: Di litrɛri imej fɔ di ol Tamil maritime prɔsperiti.
The long pillared cloister that encloses: Di lɔng kɔlɔsta we gɛt pila dɛn we de rawnd di kɔt fɔ di Brihadisvara tɛmpul, wit wan row we gɛt lingam dɛn we dɛn put nia in flɔ. Dɛn bin peint in wɔl dɛn insay di Nayak tɛm wit layf layf sinima dɛn — na ya Shiva in pɔt-bɛli gana dɛn, in ple ple dwɔf atɛndant dɛn — ɔnda wan band we gɛt Tamil kapshɔn dɛn. Bihayn dɛn kayn leta peint dɛn ya, insay di pasej we de rawnd di oli ples, na di tɛmpul in ɔrijinal Chola fresko dɛn de.
The longest of the Ten Idylls, by Mangud: Di wan we lɔng pas ɔl pan di Tɛn Idylls, we Mangudi Maruthanar rayt, we dɛn adrɛs to di Pandya kiŋ we nem Nedunchezhiyan. I de tɔk bɔt di big siti we nem Madurai frɔm do to nɛt ɛn i de mɛmba di kiŋ saful wan se ɔl di glori we de na di wɔl de pas.
The lotus pool of Sittanavasal, the Pall: Di lotus pul na Sittanavasal, di Pallava gɔd uman na Panamalai, di Chola fresko ɛn Nayak mural dɛn na di Big Tɛmpl na Thanjavur, ɛn di Tanjore peint dɛn we dɛn gild wit gold.
The Madurai Sungudi saree is a tradition: Di Madurai Sungudi saree na tradishɔnal kɔtɔn tɛkstayl we gɛt fɔ du wit Madurai, we na wan istri kɔlchɔ ɛn kɔmɛshɔn sɛnta na Tamil Nadu. I difrɛn bay di pat dɛn we gɛt dɔt, dizayn dɛn we gɛt bɔku bɔku kɔlɔ dɛn, ɛn di tradishɔnal we aw dɛn kin tay ɛn day ɔ we dɛn nɔ day. Dɛn kin tay ɔ protɛkt smɔl smɔl pat dɛn pan di klos we dɛn de day fɔ mek difrɛn pat dɛn we dɛn de opin di tin. Dɛn valyu Sungudi tɛkstayl dɛn bikɔs dɛn fayn fɔ si, dɛn gɛt kɔtɔn klos we nɔ at fɔ wɛr, ɛn dɛn fayn fɔ wɛr ɛvride ɛn fɔ di fɛstival. Di kraft de jɔyn di no bɔt aw fɔ pripia di klos, aw fɔ tay am, aw fɔ day am, ɛn aw fɔ dɔn am. I istri ɔrijin nɔ tay to wan sikrit dɔkyumɛnt stat ia. Madurai Sungudi bin gɛt GI rɛkɔgnishɔn insay 2005, we i gri se i gɛt fɔ du wit di rijɔn. Di tradishɔn de sho aw Tamil atizan dɛn bin mek difrɛn tɛkstayl dizayn dɛn we dɛn bin de yuz spɛshal daying skil dɛn ɛn lokal prodakshɔn prɔsis dɛn we dɛn bin dɔn mek.
The masonry arches that now crown the an: Di masonry arch dɛn we naw de krawn di ol weir. British injinia dɛm we bin stɔdi Kallanai insay di nayntin ia bin rili kɔle am: Shɛf Atɔ Kɔtɔn bin lan frɔm in fawndeshɔn bifo i bil di Ɔpa Anikɔt akɔdin to di Kɔlidam insay 1836, ɛn Richad Beyd Smit bin prez am insay di 1850 dɛm as wan wɔndaful wok we bin dɔn las fɔ bɔku sɛntiwɔd. Na dɛn gi am di nem “Grand Anicut”.
The Meenakshi Amman Temple, historic str: Di Meenakshi Amman Tɛmpl, istri strit dɛn, rilijɔn tradishɔn dɛn, ɛn di kɔntinyu fɔ rayt ɛn kɔlchɔ prɔsis de kɔnɛkt di mɔdan Madurai wit in lɔng istri.
The memorial hall to Karikal Chozhan at: Di mɛmorial hal fɔ Karikal Chozhan na Kallanai, we di Gɔvmɛnt fɔ Tamil Nadu rayz. Karikalan, we na di hiro fɔ di Pattinappalai ɛn di Porunararruppadai, dɛn mɛmba am na di Tamil tradishɔn as di kiŋ we bin tam di Kaveri dɛn. Leta Chola poem dɛm lɛk di Kulothunga Cholan Ula, ɛn di inskripshɔn dɛm fɔ di dinasti dɛm we se dɛn kɔmɔt frɔm am, de gi kredit to am fɔ rayz di Kaveri’s bank dɛm.
The Might of Hatred: Di Mayt we pɔsin kin et
The mini-map in the corner shows the who: Di smɔl map we de na di kɔna de sho di wan ol myuziɔm; di rɛd aro na yu, we de sho di we aw yu de fes. Opin di ful map (ɔ di Map bɔtin) ɛn pik ɛni ɔl ɔ rum fɔ travul go de.
The monuments of Mamallapuram, carved ma: Di monumɛnt dɛn na Mamallapuram, we dɛn kɔt mɔ insay di 7 ɛn 8 sɛntiwɔd C.E., inklud kev tɛmpul dɛn we dɛn kɔt wit rɔk, ratha dɛn we gɛt wan ston, ɛn di Shore Tɛmpl we gɛt strɔkchɔ. Di grup na UNESCO Wɔl Ɛritij Sayt.
The monuments themselves, with Pallava i: Di monumɛnt dɛnsɛf, wit Pallava inskripshɔn ɛn kiŋ taytul dɛn we dɛn kɔt pan dɛn.
The most celebrated of the Seven Great P: Di wan we dɛn kin sɛlibret pas ɔl pan di Sɛvin Gret Patron dɛn. Tamil tradishɔn mɛmba se i bin de gi in yon chariɔt to wan jasmin (mullai) kripa we nɔ bin gɛt natin fɔ klaym — fri-an we bin de rich pas pipul dɛn to di natura wɔl. In padi biznɛs wit di pɔyt Kapilar, in difens fɔ Parambu Nadu agens di tri kiŋ dɛn we dɛn krawn, ɛn di kray we in gyal pikin dɛn Angavai ɛn Sangavai bin kray (Purananuru 112) de kip insay Sangam poem; di chariɔt stori na di bɛst we fɔ rid am as litrɛri tradishɔn.
The mountains and the land around them,: Di mawnten dɛn ɛn di land we de rawnd dɛn, na midulnɛt insay di kol sizin. In gɔd na Murugan (Seyon), ɛn in flawa na kurinji, we kin blo wan tɛm insay twɛlv ia. I tim na punarthal, we na di sikrit mitin fɔ di wan dɛn we lɛk dɛnsɛf. I pipul dɛn kin gɛda ɔni, gayd di malet fil frɔm parrot ɛn ɔntin na di fɔrɛst.

Di Sangam Avvaiyar in poem dɛm na Purananuru, Akananuru, Kurunthogai ɛn Natrinai de tɔk bɔt kiŋ dɛm, fri-an ɛn mɔtalman layf; na bin advaysa we Adhiyaman bin abop pan. Di pikin dɛn klashik dɛn Aathichudi, Kondrai Vendhan ɛn Nalvazhi na wan leta Avvaiyar.
The Noyyal River region of Tamil Nadu pr: Di Noyyal Riva rijɔn na Tamil Nadu de gi ɔda ɛgzampul bɔt aw fɔ manej wata tru wan nɛtwɔk we gɛt tank ɛn chanɛl dɛn we gɛt fɔ du wit am. Bifo dɛn dipen pan di riva we de flɔ dairekt wan nɔmɔ, di kɔmyuniti dɛn bin mek we fɔ kip tin dɛn we go ɛp fɔ kech ɛn sheb di wata we de. Tank dɛn we de na dɛn kayn nɛtwɔk dɛn de kin gɛda di ren we kin kam insay di sizin ɛn di wata we kin rɔn, ɛn kip am fɔ yuz leta fɔ wok na fam. Di yus we dɛn bin de yuz bin dipen pan di arenjmɛnt fɔ di land, di kɔndishɔn fɔ di embankmɛnt dɛn, di kapasiti fɔ di chanɛl dɛn ɛn di tɛm we ren fɔ kam. We dɛn bin de mentɛn am fayn fayn wan, wan kɔnɛkt nɛtwɔk bin ɛp fɔ spre smɔl wata risɔs akɔdin to bɔku say dɛn. Di Noyyal Riva sistɛm de bak we dɛn no insay India in wata-ɛritij dɔkyumentri. I de sho wetin mek dɛn fɔ ɔndastand tradishɔnal irigashɔn as nɛtwɔk we gɛt rilayt strɔkchɔ dɛn pas fɔ ɔndastand tank dɛn we de ayd.
The objects of a Tamil home, the Kallana: Di tin dɛn we de na wan Tamil os, di Kallanai ɛn di vilej tank dɛn, ɛn fɔ mek fam frɔm plɔg te to avɛst.
The objects of a traditional Tamil home: Di tin dɛn we dɛn kin yuz na tradishɔnal Tamil os — kle pɔt ɛn gren jɔg, di ammi ɛn aattukkal grindin ston, di ural ɛn ulakkai, wata pɔt, ɔyl lamp, mat, fan, kɔt, baskɛt ɛn lad — ɛn di ɛvride it we dɛn kin kuk wit dɛn: rays ɛn malet, puls, koozh, bɔta milk ɛn it pan banana lif.

The palmyra palm provided several useful: Di palmyra palm bin gi bɔku yusful tin dɛn. Dɛn bin ebul fɔ it di palm sap fresh ɔ we dɛn dɔn prosɛs, ɛn dɛn bin de yuz pam shuga ɛn pam jaggery as switin. Di tin dɛn we dɛn kin mek na di palm bin valyu mɔ na di rijyɔn dɛn usay di tik bin bɔku ɛn i bin de pat pan di tin dɛn we di lokal pipul dɛn bin de liv.
The pambai is a pair of drums played tog: Di pambai na wan pe fɔ drɔm dɛn we dɛn kin ple togɛda, dɛn kɔntrast lɔw ɛn ay vɔys dɛn de drɛb pipul dɛn pɔfɔmɛnshɔn, prushɔn ɛn vilej fɛstival dɛn ɔlsay na Tamil Nadu. I liv tradishɔn bɛtɛ pas aw i kɔmɔt, ɛn in rɛptɔri de chenj frɔm rijyɔn to rijyɔn ɛn kɔmyuniti to kɔmyuniti.
The Pancha Rathas are monolithic shrines: Di Pancha Rathas na wan oli ples dɛn we dɛn kɔt ɛni wan pan dɛn frɔm wan ɔtkrɔp, we de sho bɔku bɔku tɛmpul dɛn we dɛn mek wit ston.
The Pandya capital on the Vaigai, closel: Di Pandya kapital na di Vaigai, we tay klos to di tradishɔn dɛn fɔ di Tamil Sangam ɛn klasical poem.

The parai is a Tamil frame drum: a circu: Di parai na Tamil freym drɔm: na sɛkɔral freym wit wan mɛmbran we strɛch, we dɛn kin bit wit bit dɛn we gɛt patɛn ritm. I dɔn de fɔ lɔng tɛm fɔ anɔys, ritual, fɛstival ɛn bɛrin, ɛn tide parai attam de jɔyn drɔm fɔ dans. I istri de kɛr di kasta hayarki bak we bin marginalize bɔku ɛritaj pleya dɛm — ɛn insay Tamil kɔlchɔ tide dɛn de ple di parai fɔ asɛt aydentiti, digniti ɛn ikwal.
The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea names: Di Periplus of the Erythraean Sea nem Tyndis bitwin di pɔt dɛn na di wɛst kɔst, insay di eria usay di Chɛra kiŋ bin de, ɛn Tamil buk dɛn mɛmba wan pɔt we dɛn kɔl Tondi. Usay i bin tinap nɔ shɔ: Dɛn dɔn tɔk bɔt Tanur, Ponnani ɛn Kadalundi ɔl, ɛn di mɔdan tɔŋ we nem Thondi we de na Tamil Nadu in sawt-ist kɔst nɔ kin jɔs no wit ɛvri ol rɛfrɛns. Wi kin ɔndastand Tyndis fayn fayn wan bay di ples we i de bitwin di Malabar pɔt dɛn ɛn di rod dɛn we de insay di land we de biɛn dɛn.

The reverse of a coin naming Uttama Chol: Di rivays fɔ wan kɔyn we nem Uttama Chola (c. 970–985 CE), we in silva kɔyn dɛn de pan di fɔs Chola isyu dɛn fɔ kɛr wan kiŋ in nem — ya na di Grantha skript we dɛn yuz fɔ Sanskrit na di Tamil kɔntri.
The reverse of a Setu coin, where the le: Di rivays fɔ wan Setu kɔyn, usay dɛn rayt di lay lay stori “Setu.” We yu rid di tin dɛn we dɛn rayt pan ɔl tu di fes dɛn fɔ wan kɔyn — di fɔs pat ɛn di bak pat — na aw di wan dɛn we de stɔdi bɔt mɔni kin no udat gi am ɛn ustɛm.
The revived Pandya kingdom continued to: Di Pandya kiŋdɔm we bin gɛt layf bak bin kɔntinyu fɔ yuz di fish ɛmblem, bɔku tɛm dɛn bin de sho wan pe fish, sɔm tɛm dɛn kin gɛt stik ɔ lamp.
The ripe paddy is cut by hand with sickl: Dɛn kin kɔt di rayp padi wit an wit sikɛl, dɔn dɛn kin trowe am fɔ mek di gren kɔmɔt nia di stik dɛn ɛn dɛn kin win am fɔ mek di chaf kɔmɔt. The river that fed the Chola kingdom’s a: Di riva we bin de fid di Chola kiŋdɔm in agrikalchɔral biznɛs ɛn in poem dɛn we bɔku.

The rock-cut caves, sculptural reliefs,: Di kev dɛm we dɛn kɔt wit rɔk, skapul rilif dɛm, monolitik ratha dɛm ɛn strɔkchɔral tɛmpul dɛm de gi dairekt pruf fɔ Pallava atis ajɔstmɛnt dɛm.
The Salem silk saree is associated with: Di Salem silk saree gɛt fɔ du wit Salem, we na wan impɔtant rijyɔn we dɛn de mek tɛkstayl na Tamil Nadu. Dɛn kin yuz silk yan fɔ wev dɛn saree ya, dɛn gɛt difrɛn kɔlɔ dɛn, dɛn kin mek dɛn bɔda dɛn, ɛn dɛn kin mek dɛn fayn fayn wan. Di we aw dɛn tan kin kɔmɔt frɔm simpul ɛn fayn fayn dizayn dɛn to mɔ fayn fayn klos dɛn we dɛn mek fɔ mared, fɛstival, ɛn ɔda spɛshal tɛm dɛn. Salem in tɛkstayl ɛritij gɛt fɔ du wit di big divɛlɔpmɛnt fɔ silk prodakshɔn, wef, ɛn kɔmɛshɔnal tɛkstayl makit dɛn na Tamil Nadu. Di kraft nid fɔ gɛt skilful wok fɔ pripia di stik, fɔ sɛt di loom, fɔ mek dɛn kɔntinyu fɔ wev tɛnsiɔn ɔltɛm, ɛn fɔ dɔn di klos. Salem Silk bin gɛt GI rɛkɔgnishɔn insay 2007, we fɔmal wan akɔdin to in rijinal aydentiti. Dis de fɔ rɛjista nɔ de sho ustɛm di tradishɔn bigin. Tide, Salem silk stil de pat pan Tamil Nadu in difrɛn difrɛn tɛkstayl ɛritij ɛn i de sho di impɔtant tin we rijinal wef sɛnta dɛn gɛt fɔ kip tradishɔnal skil dɛn ɛn fɔ sɔpɔt di atizan layf.

The saree traditions of Tamil Nadu — the: Di saree tradishɔn dɛn na Tamil Nadu — di silk dɛn na Kanchipuram, Arani, Thirubuvanam ɛn Salem, di tay-day kɔtɔn na Madurai Sungudi, Kovai Kora kɔtɔn, di bold chɛk dɛn na di Chettinad Kandangi, ɛn di mared saree dɛn na Koorainadu — ɛvri wan insay wan fotobuk.
The sea and the shore, at dusk in every: Di si ɛn di shore, we di ples dak insay ɛvri sizin. In gɔd na Varunan, we na di masta fɔ di wata, ɛn in flawa na di blu wata-lili (neithal). I tim na irangal — anxious pining as di heroin de wach di si fɔ in lɔvman in bot. I pipul dɛn kin fish, drɛy dɛn kech ɛn mek sɔl na di kɔstal pan dɛn.
The sea routes that joined the Tamil coa: Di si rod dɛm we bin jɔyn di Tamil kɔst to di Rɛd Si, di Mɛditarenian ɛn Sawt-Ist Eshia, di akitɛkɛt fɔ di pɔt dɛm — di wɔf dɛm, wɛl dɛm ɛn brik kway dɛm — ɛn di jɔg dɛm, pɔt ɛn guds dɛm we bin de travul bitwin dɛm — wit Adichanallur, di Ayɔn Ij bɛrin grɔn na di Thamirabarani vali, insay stil ɛn fim.
The secret of Kallanai’s endurance: clay: Di sikrit fɔ mek Kallanai ebul fɔ bia: kle ɛn di fayn fayn silt we wata bin de kɛr bin de wok insay di say dɛn we de bitwin di ston dɛn ɛn sial dɛn. The shore at Poompuhar today, near the m: Di shore na Poompuhar tide, nia di mawt fɔ di Kaveri, usay di fɔs Chola pɔt na Puhar bin de wan tɛm. Sɔv we dɛn dɔn du ɔnda wata dɔn si se dɛn dɔn mek mason na dis kɔst; aw fa di ol siti bin rich, ɛn aw di shoreline chenj, dɛn stil de stɔdi.
